description: EDDIE is a software framework for environmental digital twins with automated geospatial-data gathering, caching and updating. The Geospatial Research Institute README describes modular plugins that run models on demand and names deployments including the Flood Resilience Digital Twin. Users configure data providers and an analytical plugin; the system obtains inputs and presents a model-backed view of the chosen place. Coverage depends on the configured sources and case. GitHub metadata states AGPL-3.0 licensing. A limitation is that an automated pipeline inherits source coverage and update delays; an asset-level warning requires local data and model validation. EDDIE can couple flood and other environmental data with infrastructure assets in a digital-twin workflow. The separately maintained FReDT repository is one flood-specific application of this framework. The related QGIS catalogue platform is a general spatial desktop system. No container, geospatial data or model was downloaded.
